stories.headline: Diamondbacks miss playoffs on season's final day, losing 9-4 to Padres after Phillies clinch
stories.summary: — The Arizona Diamondbacks missed the playoffs for the eighth time in nine seasons, losing 9-4 Sunday to the postseason-bound San Diego Padres shortly after
stories.body:
SAN DIEGO -- — The Arizona Diamondbacks missed the playoffs for the eighth time in nine seasons, losing 9-4 Sunday to the postseason-bound San Diego Padres shortly after the Philadelphia Phillies won to clinch the final NL wild card spot.


The Diamondbacks (86-76) began the regular season's final day with the chance to advance if they won and the Phillies lost, but neither happened. Arizona made a six-win improvement on last season's 80-82 mark, but a stunning World Series run in 2023 remains its only postseason appearance since 2017 despite five winning records in that stretch.


Gavin Sheets homered and Freddy Fermin drove in three runs for the Padres, who rested Fernando Tatis Jr., Jackson Merrill and Xavier Bogaerts in their meaningless season finale. San Diego locked up the top NL wild card berth on Saturday before finishing 91-71, topping last year’s 90-win campaign with a club-record fifth consecutive winning season.


The Padres finished on a 17-3 surge, winning their final seven series. After sitting with a losing record in late July, the Padres will host the Chicago Cubs starting Tuesday night in their third consecutive trip to the postseason, another franchise first.


Arizona catcher Gabriel Moreno won the NL batting title despite being scratched about an hour before first pitch with a sore hamstring. Moreno became the first catcher to win a batting crown since Buster Posey in 2012, finishing at .311 — barely ahead of Philadelphia’s Luis Arraez (.310), who was out this weekend with a sprained ankle.


The Phillies led Tampa Bay 4-0 when the Diamondbacks took the field at Petco Park, and Philly never gave Arizona’s scoreboard-watchers much hope.


Randy Vásquez pitched six outstanding innings of one-run ball for San Diego, but reliever Griffin Canning (5-9) blew a three-run lead in the seventh with Corbin Carroll, Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar delivering RBI for Arizona.


Jake Cronenworth then drew a bases-loaded walk from Justin Martinez (3-1) at almost the same moment the Phillies finished their 7-3 win over Tampa Bay. Fermin added a two-run single shortly afterward.


Manny Machado singled in Sung-Mun Song in the third and then left for a pinch-runner. The slugger ended the regular season with 399 career homers, third-most among active players behind Giancarlo Stanton and Mike Trout.


Sheets led off the fourth with his 17th homer in his second game back from a four-week absence with a left foot injury.


Up next
Padres: Michael King starts Game 1 against the Cubs at Petco Park. Chicago took two of three from San Diego in the Wild Card Round last season at Wrigley Field.


------

stories.headline: Liberty push No. 1-seed Lynx to brink in stunning Game 1 upset
stories.summary: Breanna Stewart put up 34 points and 12 rebounds to help the Liberty to a Game 1 upset of the No. 1-seeded Lynx.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- When Breanna Stewart can't be stopped, playoff seedings don't matter.

The future Hall-of-Famer finished with 34 points, 12 rebounds, six assists, two steals and two blocks as she led the 8th-seeded New York Liberty to a lopsided 91-75 road victory over the Minnesota Lynx, the top seed in the WNBA playoffs and the favorite to win the title.

"[Stewart's] ability to post up: she's a walking mismatch, so we're able to just look for her," said Sabrina Ionescu, who finished with 13 points and four assists in the first game of the best-of-three series. "And obviously, whatever they take away, we have a counter. So whether it's inside, just trying to stay spaced, find the 3-point line. I also think we just took really good shots."

The Liberty, who defeated the Lynx by double figures in Minneapolis nine days before Sunday's game, can win the series and secure the upset on Tuesday in New York City. The Lynx are 0-3 in franchise history and 0-2 under Cheryl Reeve when they lose the first game in a best-of-three playoff series.

Stewart, who has averaged nearly 21 points per game against the Lynx throughout her WNBA career, led the Liberty to their third double-digit win over the Lynx in the four games they've played this season.

Stewart's success also affected the rest of her team. The Liberty connected on 52 percent of its 3-point attempts. Leonie Fiebich, who'd scored 10 points combined in four previous games, finished with 16 points (4-for-5 from beyond the arc) with the Lynx sending extra defenders at Stewart and creating space along the perimeter for her teammates. Stewart was also effective defensively. The Lynx made just 34 percent of their shots after halftime.

On the same day A'ja Wilson won her fourth Associated Press MVP award, surpassing Stewart as a three-time winner, the Liberty star offered a reminder of her standing among the WNBA greats. She became the second player in WNBA history to lead or co-lead her team in points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks in a playoff game, per ESPN Research.

She's also the fourth player in league history to finish with 30 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a playoff game.

"I think I was just really ready. I mean, if you don't get up for these big moments, then you've got to rethink why you're playing basketball," Stewart said. "But for myself, mentally, I was just ready to do whatever it took to lead the team and get the win today. And my teammates found me and got me good looks at the basket, so I just wanted to keep going."

Napheesa Collier (12 points, 6-for-14), Natasha Howard (eight points) and Nia Brodie (16 points, 4-for-5 from the 3-point line) all had four fouls in the third quarter as they collectively tried to corral Stewart. The Lynx made four of their last five 3-point attempts to end the first half but lost the momentum as they accumulated more fouls after the break.

"We did a solid job in the first half and then we just fouled, fouled, fouled. You can't give [Stewart] 12 free throws," Reeve said. "So fouling at the end of the shot clock, one second left, it's just not smart. She does a good job where she puts her body and obviously gets those calls."

But Stewart cautioned it's dangerous to get too confident based on recent history. Last year, the Liberty, a 5-seed, defeated the Phoenix Mercury in the first game of their best-of-three series before they were eliminated after losing the next two games.

"We did this in Phoenix and then we got smoked on our home court," Stewart said. "So being really intentional for the adjustments we're going to make. Obviously, we had a ton of turnovers [19] and want to be better in that area, but we're going to just have to have the same steadiness that we had for today -- we're going to do that on Tuesday."

For Minnesota, it was an extension of the murkiness this team has endured over the last month. The Lynx started the season led by Olivia Miles as their catalyst, but the favorite to win the Rookie of the Year award finished with 11 points on 3-for-12 shooting and one assist on Sunday as the team struggled to find a rhythm. Since Collier's return from multiple ankle surgeries, the Lynx have worked to solidify a new identity.

In the six games prior to Sunday's loss, the Lynx were 2-4 and 11th in offensive efficiency and eighth in defensive efficiency during that stretch, all while committing turnovers on nearly one-of-five possessions.

After the game, Reeve said she didn't want to say a lot and risk leaking Tuesday's game plan for a team that's been hailed as the favorite to win the franchise's fifth championship for months.

That plan, however, will have to include a new approach to defending one of the greatest players in WNBA history if the Lynx want to avoid an early playoff exit.

"I think that obviously when you're the lower seed, right, you want to steal one," Stewart said. "You want to steal one at their place and doing that today is obviously really important for this series. But we've kind of harped on it: this doesn't mean relax. This team is obviously really exceptionally talented and they're going to throw everything they've got at us on Tuesday and we're going to be ready for it."

stories.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
stories.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, and the Browns won their second straight game.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

SEA-WSH | CAR-CLE | CIN-PIT

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

Catch up on Thursday's game:

ATL-GB

Washington 33, Seattle 31
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Commanders
How did this happen? Turnovers and an efficient offense. The Commanders forced three turnovers, leading to three touchdowns -- two by the offense and another on a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. The offense capitalized on two short fields after a fumble and an interception, while quarterback Marcus Mariota did what was needed. He was smart with the ball, making quick throws and taking checkdowns to keep the chains moving. And he was aggressive when necessary, like on a tight-window throw to WR Trey Burks for his second touchdown. It was an unlikely win without quarterback Jayden Daniels, linebacker Frankie Luvu, tight end Chig Okonkwo, right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross.

Trend to watch: Washington did not force any turnovers in its first two games, which continued an ugly trend: Only one team has forced fewer turnovers than the Commanders since 2024. But they harped on it all offseason, and the focus paid off Sunday. Can they sustain it? It helped that they played coverage much better than they did against Dallas in Week 2. But to get more, the front needs to generate more consistent pressure. It'll help when they get blitzing linebacker Frankie Luvu back soon from a groin injury. -- John Keim

Next game: vs. Colts in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (London) p.m. ET)

Seahawks
What was most concerning about Seattle's upset loss? The defending Super Bowl champions came into this game on a 12-game winning streak, with Sam Darnold back at quarterback, and as the much healthier team. There were plenty of reasons they lost as 8.5-point favorites, but a big one was their absence of a run game -- something they could have used in the rain. Seattle's tailbacks gained just 39 yards on 17 carries. Rookie Jadarian Price lost his second fumble in as many weeks to set up Washington's first touchdown. The Seahawks got away with turnovers last season because their defense and special teams were so good. But they didn't do enough to overcome three giveaways against Washington.

What to make of the QB performance: Darnold's return from the glute injury that sidelined him for most of the first two games was a mixed bag. With no run game, he carried the offense by completing 31 of 45 attempts for 379 yards, four touchdowns and two interceptions -- one coming on a throw that was deflected at the line of scrimmage, while the other was a back-breaking pick-six in the fourth quarter. Two of Darnold's TD passes were to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, but he spread the ball around more than Drew Lock did.

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Best quote from the locker room: On his pick-six, Darnold was trying to find tight end AJ Barner, but defensive end Odafe Oweh kept him in the pocket, and Medrano jumped the short, play-action throw over the middle. "Just a bad decision," Darnold said. "The end did a good job of not letting me escape to the outside and I had to make a quick decision and I should have dirted it at his feet. ... I saw him. He made a really good play, but that's a ball I've got to throw away." -- Brady Henderson

Fantasy football takeaway: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin caught six of a team-high nine targets from Marcus Mariota, finishing with 77 yards and a touchdown (19.7 fantasy points). With this type of volume -- and clear on-field chemistry with Mariota -- McLaurin fits as a WR2/flex option for Week 4. -- Bowen

Cleveland 21, Carolina 18
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns
Is Deshaun Watson turning the corner? For the second straight week, Watson engineered a game-winning touchdown drive. This time, it helped turn around a slow start for the Browns' offense that lasted three quarters. Entering the fourth quarter, Watson was 10-for-21 for 67 yards and a touchdown. However, he has been at his best when the Browns have needed it the most. On the game-winning drive, Watson converted a pair of third downs, including his touchdown.

Key stat to know: Defensive tackle Mason Graham recorded his fourth sack in three games (two on Sunday against Bryce Young). That made him the first Browns player since Myles Garrett in 2019 to record a sack in the first three games of the season. Graham had a half-sack throughout all of last season as a rookie.

Best quote from the locker room: "We're playing for first place. Holy s---! Is that cool or what? Our guys are ready to rock and roll and we'll be good to go," coach Todd Monken exclaimed after Sunday's win. "But appreciate the fans and we're not perfect. We're not coaching or playing. We're going to fight like hell to get there, I promise." -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: vs. Steelers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Panthers
Is this offensive line sustainable until Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu return from their respective injuries? The Panthers have struggled to run the ball efficiently through three weeks. Carolina's ground attack was stifled Sunday, as running back Chuba Hubbard produced 18 yards on 10 carries in the first half; he still finished with 82 rushing yards on 19 carries. With left guard Damien Lewis forced from the game for a stretch, the line leaned on backup Corey Bullock, who didn't improve matters during his brief playing time. In addition, QB Bryce Young was sacked twice before halftime.

What to make of the QB performance: While Young led five scoring drives, his aerial attack was subdued by the Browns. He was erratic with a crowded pocket, and he benefited from a pair of roughing the passer penalties on the final drive of the first half to put points on the board. Young finished with 291 passing yards, a TD and an INT.

Best quote from the locker room: "I think we all just got to do a better job. I think we're just kind of -- I hate to say it -- one man off every time. That could be from me or anybody else," said Panthers right guard Rob Hunt of the team's run game struggles. "So we've just got to be on the same page. I think we've just got to click, and I think later in the game, it felt good and it looked good. We've got to start early. If we start early, it's a different ball game." -- Mike Kaye

Next game: vs. Lions (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Browns rookie WR Denzel Boston was a priority waiver wire add after catching a touchdown in each of his first two games. In Sunday's win, he caught only two of four targets for 41 yards (8.1 points). Boston has the explosive play ability to post a big number in the lineup, but he should be viewed as a boom/bust WR3 in a very inconsistent offense. -- Bowen

Pittsburgh 30, Cincinnati 27
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
How has CB Joey Porter Jr.'s absence impacted the Steelers? Porter was inactive for a third week in a row as he continues to "ramp up" amid his aggravated back injury and contentious contract situation. Bengals QB Joe Burrow picked on CB Asante Samuel Jr., eventually leading to rookie Daylen Everette replacing Samuel in the fourth quarter. Big-bodied receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase overpowered Samuel several times, including on Higgins' second-quarter touchdown, when the receiver boxed out the smaller Samuel. In the fourth quarter, the rookie was then part of a group responsible for a busted coverage that resulted in a Mike Gesicki touchdown.

Trend to watch: With Rico Dowdle out, running back Jaylen Warren played more than 90% of the offensive snaps -- a far cry from the balanced workload he carried with Dowdle in the first two weeks. With 17 carries for 127 yards, he showed Sunday that he's more than capable of carrying the load. It wasn't a perfect afternoon for Warren, though, as he got tripped up on the turf yards away from a breakaway touchdown late in the fourth quarter. -- Brooke Pryor

Best quote from the locker room: "It sucks that you have to have something like this happen after a loss," said LT Troy Fautanu on the offense's bounce-back performance. "Obviously you want to do this regardless if you win the week before or not, but sometimes you got to get punched in the face in order to learn."

Next game: at Browns (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Bengals
Are the Bengals playing well enough to be considered a serious contender? Sunday put a serious dent in that belief. After a good performance in all three phases against Houston, it was anything but that against the Steelers. Notably, the team had two bad special teams blunders -- a roughing the punter penalty and a muffed punt that ultimately led to 10 points. And Cincinnati's defense, while good in spots, gave up significant yardage after the catch, including on a late 47-yard reception by tight end Darnell Washington. The Steelers finished with 411 yards.

What to make of the QB performance: It was good up until the end. Burrow probably tried to do a bit too much trying to extend a play late and coughed up the ball with the Bengals driving for a potential tie or win. He completed his first 14 passes of the game and threw three touchdown passes, including a key fourth-down conversion that kept Cincinnati's hopes of winning alive. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Warren took on a volume role with Rico Dowdle out with a toe injury, scoring a season-high 20.6 fantasy points. If Dowdle has to sit again in Week 4, Warren can be played as a midtier RB2. -- Bowen

N.Y. Giants 12, Tennessee 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
Did Jameis Winston do enough to inspire confidence as Giants QB? It wasn't perfect, but a win is a win. Winston did enough to help the Giants beat a struggling Titans team. His accuracy was off early, but he made some big plays throughout the game, especially on the opening drive of the second half. He finished 14-of-22 for 118 yards. It should be enough for him to remain the starter, and the Giants are still intent on adding another QB. Jimmy Garoppolo, J.J. McCarthy and Gardner Minshew are the most likely options.

Trend to watch: Running back Najee Harris' role increases. The veteran had four carries in his debut last week and nine Sunday for 52 yards. Harris jump-started the Giants' offense with six carries for 36 yards on their first drive of the second half. It should increase his playing time and role moving forward. Starter Cam Skattebo had 23 touches for 100 yards.

Best quote from the locker room: "That was a great win," Skattebo said. "A year ago, we lose that game 100%." -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: vs. Cardinals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Titans
Are the Titans playing like the worst team in the league? The Titans' offense was downright miserable for most of the game. Quarterback Cam Ward failed to see open receivers on multiple plays and missed Carnell Tate for what should have been an easy touchdown. They opened with five consecutive three-and-outs and finally got a first down late in the third quarter. The series of three-and-outs came after Chimere Dike fumbled the opening kickoff. It was a respectable effort by the defense, but Ward's inexplicable pass late in the fourth resulted in an interception and a Titans loss.

Trend to watch: Time of possession was an issue for the third game. At one point, the Giants held a 28:15 to 9:49 edge. The Titans managed to drive 91 yards in seven minutes late in the fourth quarter for their first points to help cut the deficit in time of possession and the overall score. The final drive, which ended in an interception, made it 34:26 to 25:34. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Ravens (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Giants WR Malik Nabers is struggling terribly with QB Jaxson Dart sidelined. Nabers' 7.6 fantasy points gives him two of the four worst fantasy scores of his career in the past two weeks. Nabers might have difficulty delivering even WR2 value without a QB upgrade. -- Cockcroft

Buffalo 24, L.A. Chargers 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bills
How did the Bills remain undefeated after committing five turnovers? Five turnovers, 10 penalties, two dropped interceptions and four sacks allowed. Quarterback Josh Allen's passer rating was barely north of 50. The Bills had no right to have kept this one close, but despite that the game never spun out of control. These battled-tested Bills somehow avoided spiraling or pressing. Give the defense its flowers, but the real impressive trend was the team's overall composure in the face of mistake after mistake to keep the win in reach.

Key stat to know: This was the first time the Bills won a game with a minus-four turnover differential since 1997. The opposing quarterback that afternoon was Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh. That was also the last time the Bills won any game in which they turned the ball over five times. -- Nick Suss

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Chargers
How concerning is Justin Herbert's start to the season? The defense tried its best to give Herbert and the offense a chance to win. Herbert -- who could have easily had three interceptions -- ended up throwing just one, and yet, the interception to C.J. Gardner-Johnson was a dagger. Herbert's play wasn't the only issue, as there were dropped passes and questionable playcalls. But ultimately, he hasn't looked like the superstar he was during the first six years of his career.

Most surprising performance: The Chargers' defense. Five turnovers typically means a win in the NFL. Somehow, it didn't on this day. Nevertheless, putting a lid on the league's best offense was encouraging. This is a unit that struggled against Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. So the Chargers should feel encouraged that their defense -- which has been the top unit the past two seasons -- is back. -- Kris Rhim

Next game: at Seahawks (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's grip on the primary running back role no longer ironclad? He barely edged Keaton Mitchell in snap share (42% to 36%) and total touches (15 to 11). Mitchell also had the better underlying metrics, hinting at more sharing moving forward. Add Mitchell, who is available in 84.4% of ESPN leagues. -- Cockcroft

Indianapolis 19, Houston 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Colts
Has the Colts' defense stopped the bleeding? The Colts entered this game ranked last in several major defensive categories, including a staggering 1,029 yards allowed in the first two weeks -- second most in NFL history. On Sunday, the missed assignments that led to wide-open receivers in the first two games and the flurry of missed tackles seemed to be mostly addressed. The Colts also took advantage of Houston's porous pass protection to consistently pressure Texans QB C.J. Stroud. Whether this was a one-week reprieve or the start of a trend, the Colts needed this.

What to make of the QB performance: Daniel Jones did not play smart in this game, as at least two of his three turnovers could be attributed to his own decisions. Jones' interception came when he threw a desperation pass while under pressure in field goal range. He also fumbled in the fourth quarter after not protecting the ball despite having multiple pass rushers converging on him. He did make some clutch throws on the game-winning drive. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: vs. Commanders in London (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (London) p.m. ET)

Texans
Is it time to panic on the Texans' 2026 season? It's trending that way. Even though the Texans' defense forced three turnovers (two in the second half) and had clutch plays from Stroud on their second-to-last drive to take the lead, it wasn't enough. Yes, the Texans started 0-3 last season and recovered, but that is not sustainable again. No team in NFL history has ever overcome 0-3 starts in back-to-back seasons, so expecting Houston to do that again is unrealistic.

Trend to watch: Houston's defense had zero turnovers coming into Week 3, but forced three, which gave them a chance to win. That's the type of playmaking defense Houston wants. And they're going to need it to dig themselves out of this hole. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: vs. Cowboys (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Colts WR Keenan Allen scored 18.3 fantasy points, stepping up as a short-route target over the middle while Alec Pierce (heel) heals. Daniel Jones' area of strength has come in the short game so far this season, so Allen shapes up as a matchup-dependent fantasy WR3 in the short term. -- Cockcroft

Detroit 31, N.Y. Jets 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Have the Lions fixed their defensive issues after rough start to season? After giving up 71 points through the first two weeks, Detroit shook up its secondary with Rock Ya-Sin serving a reserve role, while CB Roger McCreary started at outside cornerback alongside veteran D.J. Reed. Entering the game, the Lions were outgained by 191 total yards, fifth worst in the NFL, but second-year defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard refused to do any finger-pointing. Instead, he held a Monday meeting to dissect the struggles. The unit responded with a key takeaway in crunch time, but the defense still has major work to do.

Key stat to know: Jahmyr Gibbs finished with three total TDs, but his two rushing touchdowns helped him surpass Billy Sims (42) for the second-most rushing TDs (43) in franchise history -- trailing only Barry Sanders (99). Sanders was in attendance as part of the Lions' alumni homecoming. Gibbs put on a show in front of the Hall of Famer, finishing with 20 carries for 99 rushing yards and seven catches for 65 receiving yards. -- Eric Woodyard

Next game: at Panthers (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Jets
Why can't the Jets win close games? Another week, another crushing loss. The Jets had a chance to steal one in Motown, but their defense -- ranked No. 1 in yards allowed heading into the game -- imploded in crunch time. They let the Lions march 65 yards on four plays for the winning touchdown with 2:20 left in the fourth quarter, thanks to blown coverages on two pass plays. Then QB Geno Smith fumbled on the ensuing possession. Good teams rise up in the clutch; the Jets haven't mastered that yet. They blew a 10-point lead last week and lost in overtime. This week, a 14-point comeback wasn't enough.

Trend to watch: Rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq has arrived. It took only three games for the first-round pick to establish himself as a versatile target. He caught seven passes for 105 yards, including a 24-yard touchdown on a diving play in the end zone. Sadiq now has a receiving TD and a rushing TD (Week 1) in his first three games. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Bears (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Sadiq displayed his seam-stretching ability in a positive matchup versus the Lions' secondary, scoring a career-best 23.5 points. Available in over 65% of ESPN leagues, he should be added this week. But Sadiq should still be viewed only as a deeper league starter. -- Bowen

Jacksonville 35, New England 6
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Jaguars
Do the Jaguars even need Travis Hunter to play offense? After three weeks, Hunter has one catch and one carry. He hasn't touched the ball on offense since the opener. Hunter played five offensive snaps Sunday, giving him 16 for the season. But the Jaguars have scored 82 points, rookie WR Josh Cameron has emerged, and QB Trevor Lawrence is having success spreading the ball around. The run game cranked up against New England, too (135 yards). Why force Hunter on the field if the offense is rolling without him?

Most surprising performance: The Jaguars gave Cameron a bigger role in Week 3, and he delivered with a touchdown catch (second on three catches this season) and a 42-yard kickoff return. Through three quarters versus the Patriots, he had nearly as many snaps on offense (16) as Brian Thomas Jr. (21) -- an indication that more work could be ahead as the season progresses.

Best quote from the locker room: Hunter on his end zone interception: "I know [Maye] tried me a couple times, so I was just in there saying, 'I'm getting too close to the ball. I got to get me one.' So we just continued to just do what the coaches schemed up for us and we just played our best part of it." -- Mike DiRocco

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Patriots
What can the Patriots do to get Drake Maye back on track? Maye's 2026 woes continued with his 10th game of multiple turnovers (tied for most in NFL since 2024). The end zone interception just before halftime, on third-and-goal from the 2-yard line, was a shocking decision as WR Efton Chism III was tightly covered by Travis Hunter. It was a play similar to Maye's miscue in the season-opening loss at Seattle. In the first half, Maye was pressured 11 times -- his most before halftime in his career -- and went 2-of-7 with an interception and two sacks, per ESPN Research.

Trend to watch: Offensive line injuries. Veteran Greg Van Roten, who started at right guard in place of Mike Onwenu (broken ankle), didn't return after leaving the game in the second quarter (thigh). Walter Rouse, who was acquired in a trade with the Vikings in August, took over for Van Roten.

Best quote from the locker room: Maye on the biggest difference from last season: "I think it's getting out of my own way. These mistakes that I'm making personally are really [not] them beating us, it's me beating myself. ... This league will humble you quick." -- Mike Reiss

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Though Chris Rodriguez Jr. scored, Bhayshul Tuten continued to flash his elite speed, scoring 17.0 fantasy points on 17 touches. Tuten's 48% snap share and usage offer encouragement that he can be a weekly fantasy RB2. (And, for what it's worth, sit Maye next week at Buffalo. Please.) -- Cockcroft

Kansas City 24, Miami 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Despite winning, should the Chiefs be concerned about their pass rush? Entering Week 3, no NFL QB had been sacked more than Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (nine). The fact that the Chiefs couldn't pressure him while not blitzing was similar to the pass-rush struggles of last season, when defensive tackle Chris Jones was the lone major presence. On Sunday, defensive end George Karlaftis was the lone defender to record a hit on Willis. The Chiefs won't beat better opponents with a similar performance. The Chiefs also didn't sack Colts quarterback Daniel Jones last week -- and that game ended in overtime.

Stat to know: Running back Kenneth Walker III is the first player to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within his team's first three games of a season since 2017, when former running back Todd Gurley was a member of the Rams. Walker is also the first player in Chiefs history to accomplish the feat. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Raiders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
Have the Dolphins begun to turn the page on both sides of the ball? On defense, absolutely. The Dolphins kept the game in front of them, forced turnovers and rallied after an ugly first two drives. Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez recorded his first career takeaway and looked like a future star. The Chiefs' offense made plenty of mistakes, but Miami flew to the ball and limited explosives for the most part. Meanwhile, the Dolphins' passing game looked sharper than it has all season, but they struggled to run the ball after De'Von Achane was injured on the opening drive. We will see if Miami can build on this next week.

What to make of the QB performance: Willis completed 20 of 36 passes for 210 yards in possibly his best performance of the season. Unlike his previous two games, Willis made quicker decisions with the football and was far more willing to take off if receivers weren't open. That being said, his accuracy waned at times, and he missed a few deep shots. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: at Vikings (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon II played 83% of the offensive snaps after Achane's injury, recording 20 touches and 14.5 fantasy points. The Dolphins would probably activate Jaylen Wright for depth next week, but Gordon should be a priority pickup if Achane's prognosis for Week 4 is iffy. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas criticises Man City's alleged rule breaches: 'Equal rules for all'
stories.summary: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential.
stories.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has said Manchester City legal battle against the Premier League shows why "equal rules for all" are essential to protect football's integrity and sustainability.

ESPN reported on Friday that a source has confirmed City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

- Ogden: Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

In 2020, Man City succeeded in overturning a two-year European competition ban from UEFA at the Court of Arbitration, after being found to have breached the governing body's Financial Fair Play (FFP) rule.

Tebas had previously spoken out against "so-called financial doping in European football".

In a lengthy post on X, Tebas reflected on those statements he had given during the Soccerex event, which had been held in Manchester during September 2017.

Tebas also called the CAS ruling a "deeply misguided decision" which was "extraordinarily damaging to the credibility of European football's economic control system" and again stressed the same rules must apply to all clubs.

"Economic sustainability is not bureaucracy. Financial control is not a whim," he said.

"And arguing that clubs should compete fundamentally with the resources they are able to generate doesn't mean being against any specific club either. It's about defending a model.

"A model in which sporting success doesn't depend on who has the most powerful financial backing behind them, but on who manages best, generates more resources, builds better teams, and respects the same rules as everyone else.

"Defending this position has cost me a lot of criticism and not a few headaches. But I still think exactly the same as I did in Manchester in 2017.

"There are principles worth defending, even if they come at a cost. And this one, for me, is one of them.

- Man City chairman on club's Premier League charges case: 'Nothing has changed'

"Now, almost nine years after those words at Soccerex, an independent Premier League commission has deemed 114 of the 115 financial breaches charged against Manchester City proven, according to the published reports.

"There's still a way to go. The sanction remains to be known, and the process isn't over. But what's happened once again shows why economic control, transparency, and equal rules for all are essential to protect the integrity and sustainability of football."

"We will keep defending those principles. Just like in 2017."

Information from PA contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Islanders sign Logan Stanley to one-year contract
stories.summary: The Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.
stories.body:
The New York Islanders have signed Logan Stanley to a one-year contract, adding the defenseman days before their season opener.

They added the 28-year-old left-handed shooter late in training camp after sending Kashawn Aitcheson and Isaiah George to their American Hockey League affiliate in Hamilton. George was considered a possibility to win a full-time roster spot at 22 after playing four games last season and 33 in 2024-25.

The No. 18 overall pick in 2016 by the Winnipeg Jets, Stanley was dealt to the Buffalo Sabres last season at the trade deadline. He finished the season with seven goals and 26 points, both career highs, while finishing a two-year, $2.5 million contract.

But Stanley struggled in the postseason and was scratched in Buffalo's final four games of a Round 2 loss to the Montreal Canadiens. He skated in eight playoff contests, accumulated 19 penalty minutes and finished with a minus-2 rating.

The Islanders, who have missed the playoffs the past two seasons and brought in Peter DeBoer as their new head coach, open the regular season Wednesday at the Toronto Maple Leafs.

A left-shot defenseman who is a native of Kitchener, Ontario, Stanley has international experience playing for Team Canada. In 2016, he played in the world junior championships, when Canada finished fourth.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
stories.summary: The Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash.
stories.body:
The Chicago Bulls have traded Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Sunday.

Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in the 2024 NBA draft and still just 21 years old, was moved less than a year after landing in Chicago at the trade deadline last season. He appeared in 30 games for the Bulls, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists.

He could have a chance for a larger role in Charlotte, which traded longtime starting guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves earlier this offseason. Dillingham also joins the Hornets after Charlotte announced Friday that second-year guard Kon Knueppel has been sidelined with a hamstring injury.

The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the deal.

Hield spent less than a week with the Hornets, who acquired the veteran sharpshooter from the Atlanta Hawks for Dorian Finney-Smith. Hield, known as a positive and high-energy player, has history with Bulls executive vice president Bryson Graham from their time together in New Orleans.

Dillingham has one more year via a team option on his rookie contract before hitting restricted free agency in the summer of 2028. Hield has a player option worth around $10 million for the 2027-28 season.

stories.headline: Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search
stories.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello.
stories.body:
Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur has expressed frustration over the persistent speculation about his future at Maranello, which was only amplified earlier this week when former Red Bull boss Christian Horner stated his desire to take the top job at Ferrari.

Vasseur signed a multi-year contract to continue as Ferrari team principal last year, but it has done little to quieten rumours that his future beyond the end of this season could be in doubt.

Ferrari has won two races this year and is currently second in the constructors' standings -- albeit 160 points adrift of championship leaders Mercedes.

The Italian team has not scored a podium in the last five races, adding to the pressure on Vasseur, while Horner was quoted in an interview on Thursday saying the team principal role at Ferrari would be "the dream."

Horner was fired from his position as CEO and team principal at Red Bull last year but has made no secret of his desire to return to F1.

He stated previously that he would only return to F1 in a position that also includes a shareholding in a team, but in Thursday's interview said he would make an exception for Ferrari.

When asked about Horner's comments, Vasseur vented his frustration about the constant speculation around his future.

"We are not working in the perfect serenity," Vaseeur was quoted as saying by The Race following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. "For me firstly, but for everybody in the team.

"For the media, for 50% of the questions [to be] about this, I think it's a bit of a frustrating situation.

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

- George Russell warns 'pressure' is on Kimi Antonelli after 'most dominant weekend in my career'

"We are fighting for P2 in the championship, and at the end of the day, we are all speaking a lot about this, and even for the guys in the garage, to discuss about this, it's the best discussion that we can have.

"But it is what it is, it's not in my hands. Mr Horner is looking for a job -- that everybody knows -- everywhere.

"But what can I do? Just try to do my best to push the team, to rise them to be motivated, focus on what is better today.

"Each interview, 25 times a day, we are coming back to this."

He added: "But it is like it is. We have still seven races to go, and I will push until the last corner."

Following a sixth-place finish at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Lewis Hamilton was asked by Sky Sports if he is still confident Ferrari is on a "good path" with Vasseur in charge, to which he simply responded: "Yes."

In a follow-up question Hamilton was asked if the team still had "good unity," and again he responded: "Yep."

Finally, when asked what the team can do over the remaining races, Hamilton said: "Keep trying."

stories.headline: What We Learned: Twelve-man Knights defy belief; Smith books Roosters reunion
stories.summary: The Newcastle Knights have completed one of the most remarkable turnarounds in NRL history, stunning minor premiers Penrith. Three things we learned.
stories.body:
Accor Stadium, SYDNEY -- From wooden spooners to Grand Finalists.

The Newcastle Knights have completed one of the most remarkable turnarounds in NRL history, stunning minor premiers Penrith 20-14 despite playing the final 44 minutes with 12 men.

Phoenix Crossland was sent off for the hip-drop tackle which left Nathan Cleary with a serious leg injury, but the Knights overturned an eight-point half-time deficit to reach their first Grand Final since 2001.

They will now face the Sydney Roosters, setting up an extraordinary reunion for former Tricolours halfback Sandon Smith.

Here are three things we learned from Sunday's preliminary final.

NEWCASTLE'S FAIRYTALE IS NOW SO MUCH MORE

This is no longer a fairytale.

Newcastle's place in the Grand Final was earned through courage, resilience and sheer defiance.

The Knights had every reason to fall apart after Crossland's dismissal in the 36th minute. Their hooker was gone, Penrith had an extra man and Blaize Talagi's ensuing penalty goal handed the Panthers the lead.

When Lindsay Smith crashed over shortly before halftime, Penrith led 14-6 and appeared ready to clinically dismantle another challenger.

Instead, the Knights produced a second half that will live permanently in the club's history.

Dominic Young finished one of the tries of the season just three minutes after the restart, handling twice in a sweeping movement that began inside Newcastle's half and also involved Sandon Smith, Dane Gagai and Francis Manuleleua.

It was a statement of intent. The Knights were not going to spend the remainder of the contest desperately protecting their line and waiting for Penrith to finish them.

Even when they were forced into survival mode, their scramble was extraordinary.

Kalyn Ponga and Manuleleua held Casey McLean up by millimetres. Greg Marzhew rushed in to pressure a pass intended for an unmarked Brian To'o. Dylan Lucas followed an error with a shot that forced Lindsay Smith to spill the ball, while Ponga folded Moses Leota with one of the defining tackles of the afternoon.

Newcastle defended their two-point advantage for more than 20 minutes despite playing a man down, then sealed the result through Smith at the death.

This was not a fortunate side falling into a Grand Final.

The Knights eliminated South Sydney, survived a sold-out Eden Park and then conquered the minor premiers with 12 men.

Justin Holbrook inherited the wooden spooners less than 12 months ago. He now has Newcastle 80 minutes from a premiership.

SANDON SMITH HAS EARNED THE ULTIMATE REUNION

Of all the possible Grand Final storylines, Sandon Smith facing his former club might be the most compelling.

Smith left the Roosters at the end of last season in search of the opportunity to control his own side. On Sunday, he proved he is capable of controlling the biggest games.

With Newcastle trailing 14-10 after an hour, Penrith conceded a penalty for high contact on Fletcher Sharpe.

As Billy Phillips and Moses Leota turned their backs and waited for the kick to touch, Smith saw something nobody else did.

He tapped the ball, accelerated through a vacant defensive line and raced 50 metres untouched to score beneath the posts.

Penrith were furious. Newcastle were level. Smith calmly converted his own try to put the Knights ahead.

It was a moment of audacity from a halfback who refused to allow the occasion, or his side's numerical disadvantage, to make him conservative.

Smith then produced the decisive play in the dying moments, securing possession and racing away for the try which finally ended Penrith's resistance.

His impact extended beyond the scoreboard.

With Crossland dismissed and Fletcher Sharpe enduring some untidy moments, Smith became Newcastle's organiser, primary kicker and calming presence. He repeatedly drove Penrith into their own corners and trusted his depleted defensive line to keep turning the Panthers away.

The 23-year-old will now enter a grand final against the club where his NRL career began.

The Roosters know better than anyone what Smith can do.

They will now have to stop him from completing one of rugby league's great revenge stories.

PENRITH'S LOSS FEELS SECONDARY TO CLEARY'S INJURY

Nathan Cleary entered the contest under an injury cloud and began the match on the bench as Penrith attempted to manage a stress-related issue in his foot.

He entered after 26 minutes.

Ten minutes later, Penrith's season, and potentially the immediate future of their champion halfback, was turned upside down.

Cleary became trapped in a tackle involving Crossland and Manuleleua, with Crossland's weight falling across the playmaker's lower leg.

The reaction was immediate. Cleary remained on the turf in severe distress as medical staff rushed onto the field, before he was taken from Accor Stadium on a medicab and transported to hospital.

Early reports indicated a suspected compound fracture, while Crossland was sent off for the hip-drop tackle.

The confronting incident left players from both teams visibly shaken and stripped the preliminary final of much of its celebratory atmosphere.

Penrith's injury toll worsened in the 67th minute when Talagi went down without contact and was assisted from the field with a suspected Achilles injury.

The Panthers still had enough opportunities to win.

McLean was held up centimetres short. Jack Cogger dropped the ball at second receiver with Penrith attacking. Luke Garner's pass to an unmarked To'o was called forward, and several other promising sets ended with basic errors.

Those moments will frustrate Ivan Cleary. Penrith played more than half the match with an extra man and failed to score a single point after the break.

For so long, their defining quality has been an ability to remain composed while opponents unravel around them. On Sunday, confronted by injuries, a desperate defensive line and a Knights side with nothing to lose, Penrith became the frantic team.

Their second consecutive preliminary-final defeat confirms that the seemingly automatic march to grand final day is over.

For now, however, the end of Penrith's season is not the greatest concern.

The health of their champion halfback is.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Key questions, takeaways from Sunday's Game 1s
stories.summary: How New York pulled out the win against Minnesota, plus more from Sunday's first-round games.
stories.body:
The highly anticipated 2026 WNBA playoffs are here -- and they tipped off with an all-timer! The 8-seeded New York Liberty defeated the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx in Game 1 of their best-of-three first-round series. The Lynx are now on the brink of elimination and hoping to pull out a win Tuesday in New York to take this series to a Game 3.

Meanwhile, there will be three more first-round games Sunday: No. 3 Las Vegas Aces vs. No. 6 Indiana Fever (4 p.m. ET, ABC), No. 4 Atlanta Dream vs. No. 5 Washington Mystics (7 p.m., Prime Video) and No. 2 Golden State Valkyries vs. No. 7 Dallas Wings (9 p.m., USA Network/CNBC).

ESPN experts Kendra Andrews, Kareem Copeland, Alexa Philippou and Michael Voepel dissect how each game was won as well as keys for the rest of the first round of the playoffs and beyond.

MORE: Playoff predictions | Strengths, flaws for every team |

Top 25 players | Schedule

(1) Minnesota Lynx vs.

(8) New York Liberty
Final: New York 91, Minnesota 75

How the game was won: Despite an up-and-down season that ultimately led to the eighth seed in the WNBA playoffs, the Liberty still have one of the best players in basketball history. Breanna Stewart's run of dominance continued against the Lynx with a 34-point, 12-rebound effort -- her third career 30-point playoff double-double. But her impact doesn't show up just in the box score; it shows up in all of the defensive issues she creates for opponents. Case in point: Early in the third quarter, Minnesota's Napheesa Collier, Natasha Howard and Nia Brodie (4-for-5 from the 3-point line) each had four fouls. They were hesitant on defense, and Stewart capitalized. Despite drawing extra defenders, she created more looks for herself and her teammates on the perimeter (the Liberty made 52% of their shots from beyond the arc). Nine days after beating the Lynx by 12 points in Minneapolis, the Liberty did it again, more dominantly.

What it means for the Liberty: The Liberty won Game 1 behind a strong effort from Stewart, who creates matchup problems for everyone on the floor. If she can continue to be an effective presence in the paint against the Lynx (she has averaged 20.9 points per game against the franchise during her career), she'll create more opportunities for teammates, as the Lynx can't afford to put just one defender on her. Leonie Fiebich, who had scored 10 points combined in the final four games of the regular season, was a surprising beneficiary of the attention the Lynx put on Stewart on Sunday. She finished with 16 points (4-for-5 from beyond the arc).

One area to watch for the Liberty: They could have been more effective defending the 3-point line early in the game. The Lynx stayed alive because they had open looks from the perimeter. On Sunday, however, New York looked like the better team.

Who needs to step up for Minnesota? The favorites to win the 2026 WNBA title, the Lynx are on the brink of elimination and have to avoid the foul trouble that plagued them Sunday. They can't afford to have Howard and Collier in foul trouble. But the biggest X factor in Game 2 (Tuesday, 8:30 p.m. ET) will be AP Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles. All season, Minnesota played its best basketball with Miles as the maestro. But on Sunday, she looked like a rookie in her first WNBA playoff game. She was looking for chances to impact the game rather than taking control -- which is how she'd helped keep the Lynx at the top of the regular-season standings while Collier recovered from injury -- and ultimately finished with 11 points on 3-of-12 shooting. If Miles isn't the Miles she has been all season in her phenomenal rookie campaign, the Lynx could go home much earlier than anyone anticipated. -- Myron Medcalf

Game 1 previews

Top-seeded Minnesota hasn't looked dominant in recent weeks. What are the biggest concerns the Lynx have?

Philippou: Coach Cheryl Reeve has had some memorable news conferences this year, including Aug. 6 after Minnesota's loss to the Sparks when she said, "We lost our game because we don't play any f---ing defense. So, if you want to talk about offense, you sound like the players." Reeve has not been pleased with the team's defensive performance since early July, with its rating on that side of the floor ranking seventh in the league in that span (it was No. 1 in the WNBA in May and June). Reeve was even upset about the team's defensive effort in its penultimate regular-season game against the Connecticut Sun; the Lynx bounced back in a big way by holding the Fever to 66 points on Thursday. Undoubtedly, Reeve will be keeping a close eye on the defense starting in this first-round series against the Liberty -- hardly a typical No. 8 seed -- but also for the rest of the postseason should the Lynx advance.

Voepel: Consistency was Minnesota's hallmark for much of the season, but that changed in late August. The Lynx lost four of their last six regular-season games, with two of those losses coming before the FIBA World Cup break and two after. Minnesota averaged 90.8 points this season, but only 76.3 in those four losses. If the Lynx fall short of a title, it might be due to their offense not producing at the level it did for much of the regular season. As Alexa said, Reeve has placed the blame on defense, saying the problems there have slowed down the offense. But in Minnesota's last six regular-season games, Napheesa Collier averaged just 13.0 points. Collier, who was out until July 22 after ankle surgery, needs to return to her superstar scoring form.

Copeland: The Lynx would like to see Collier take another step forward in her return from surgery. Collier said last week that she feels as good as she has all season, and she's trying to get as close to 100% as possible. The five-time All-Star is moving better and quicker and is a veteran in Cheryl Reeve's system, but Collier acknowledged that getting used to the tendencies of Olivia Miles and Natasha Howard has been a learning experience. The Indiana Fever held Collier to single-digit scoring performances in the last two regular-season games, and the Lynx need her to be a bit closer to her typical dominant self.

Andrews: Miles' status is a bit concerning. She missed the last two regular-season games because of a left calf injury, and though the Lynx say it's not serious and she will play in the postseason, those soft tissue injuries are tricky. Players usually have to wait until it's fully healed, and playing on it before it's 100% could cause more damage. Perhaps Minnesota was playing it safe by holding out Miles so she would be healthy for Game 1. But, either way, the Lynx need her on the floor -- and they need her at her best -- for a deep run.

Which team has the most momentum and which has the least entering the playoffs?

Copeland: The Mystics are a league-best 16-4 since July 20. Their current four-game win streak is the second longest in the WNBA. (The Aces are on a seven-game win streak, but that run doesn't include a victory vs. a playoff team.) Washington mixed in a season-defining 93-77 win against the Fever less than a week ago. The Mystics are the youngest team in league history to reach the postseason and are having unexpected success for Year 2 of a rebuild. Washington has leaned on its defense, which has the No. 2 rating in the league (103.3) while allowing the second-fewest points (82.7).

Philippou: Since the WNBA season resumed after the World Cup break, the Atlanta Dream have led the league in net rating (31.2, albeit in just four games). Their 4-0 record in that span includes two road wins over the Liberty, one of which was without Breanna Stewart. Las Vegas and Washington are the only other undefeated teams in September, and the Lynx, Liberty and Fever are each 2-2. That Minnesota is 2-4 in its final six regular-season games is of note: Only one team in league history -- the 2021 Chicago Sky -- won the Finals after finishing with a losing record in their final six games of the regular season.

If the top-seeded Lynx don't win the title, which team will?

Philippou: History tells us that the champion will likely be the No. 1 or No. 2 seed, which this year means the Lynx or Valkyries. In this current playoff format, only one team outside the top 2 seeds has won the WNBA title: the 2021 Sky, who were a No. 6 seed and faced the fifth-seeded Mercury in the Finals. That was also the only time in this format that any teams outside the top-four seeds even reached the Finals. Still, with how tight the standings have been this year -- the top-four seeds are all separated by three games, the top six by five, and Nos. 5-8 by two -- maybe precedent goes out the window.

Copeland: The road to a title still goes through Las Vegas, and any championship hopeful will have to pry the trophy from A'ja Wilson. The league's active dynasty has won three of the past four titles and been to four Finals since 2020. Wilson, the four-time MVP and two-time Finals MVP, was a rookie the last time the Aces didn't at least reach the semifinals. The loss of starting forward NaLyssa Smith (noncontact left leg injury) was a significant blow, but the trio of Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray -- a combined 10 championships, 17 All-Star appearances and six gold medals -- has found success with different supporting casts. History is also on the line as the Aces can tie the Houston Comets, Seattle Storm and Minnesota Lynx with a league-record four titles.

Which player might have the biggest impact on the postseason?

Philippou: I have my eye on Miles, who will be appearing in her first WNBA postseason, while dealing with a calf injury that kept her out of the Lynx's last two regular-season games. She has been even better than expected as a rookie and has had some clutch regular-season performances. But how will that translate in the postseason and in a series setting where opponents have more opportunities to adjust to her? Perhaps it won't have any bearing, but in her one Elite Eight game during her college career, Miles and TCU suffered a blowout loss to South Carolina.

Copeland: Is it Jackie Young's turn for a Finals MVP? Wilson has two, and Gray got hers in 2022. Young averaged career highs in points (18.9), assists (6.8) and 3-pointers made (2.3) this season, and was fourth in the league in assists and 10th in points. Young is one of the best two-way guards in the world, and the Aces need her to play like it. Remember, she had 32 points and 10 assists in the Game 5 overtime closeout against the Fever in the 2025 semifinals, then averaged 20.3 points, six assists and five rebounds in the Finals sweep over the Mercury.

Voepel: It might seem boring to pick A'ja Wilson, but the best player in women's basketball has consistently been great in the postseason. Wilson remains hungry for championships and has an enormous impact offensively and defensively.

Andrews: I am really excited to see Angel Reese in her first postseason. She racked up double-doubles during the year, but it seems as though she has played at a different level the last week of the season. Unlike Wilson or Young, Reese doesn't have a plethora of postseason experience, but the way she has elevated the Dream this season is undeniable. They look primed to make a big playoff push, and she has been one of their most critical players.

Which first-round series are you most excited for, and what storyline are you most looking forward to seeing throughout the playoffs?

Philippou: The star power in the Aces-Fever series is historic: Per Elias, two of the three highest-scoring duos in league history will be competing against each other in the first round: Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell have combined for 47.0 points per game this year, and Jackie Young and A'ja Wilson are averaging a combined 45.1 points. It's wild to think that either Mitchell-Clark-Aliyah Boston or Wilson-Young-Chelsea Gray will not advance to the semifinals, but that's the nature of the playoffs for you.

Voepel: The Aces-Fever series is atop the marquee for the reasons Alexa stated. It also will be interesting to see how two of the youngest teams in the playoffs -- Washington and Atlanta -- compete against each other. The Dream have not advanced to the semifinals since 2018, when the Mystics beat them. Washington last made the semis in 2019, when it went on to win the WNBA title. Atlanta's Angel Reese and Washington's Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen, all members of the winning U.S. World Cup team, will make their playoff debuts.

Copeland: New York's inconsistencies have people questioning the Liberty, but this is still a first-round rematch of the 2024 Finals, which went to overtime in Game 5. The majority of the key figures are still here -- Breanna Stewart, Jonquel Jones, Sabrina Ionescu, Napheesa Collier, Kayla McBride, Courtney Williams. Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve acknowledged a respectful yet "healthy dislike" for each other. That sounds like a lot of fun for a high-stakes, three-game series. But the Aces' quest for a fourth championship and A'ja Wilson's continued persistence to surpass every other all-time great remain the storyline for me.

Andrews: I agree with Kareem's first pick: Lynx versus Liberty. Yes, it's a 2024 Finals rematch. Yes, it's a collection of the best players in the league. But I feel these teams have the most to lose. If the Lynx fail to get out of the first round, they will face a plethora of offseason questions, including why they couldn't get the job done again despite being the No. 1 seed. If the Liberty lose, it will be their second straight year not advancing out of the first round. A year ago, that cost Sandy Brondello her job, and it will surely raise more questions for New York this year.

stories.headline: Commanders' jab at Seahawks after upset leads Week 3 trolls
stories.summary: The Washington Commanders followed up their upset victory over the Seattle Seahawks with a petty post.
stories.body:
Sometimes, upset wins bring the best out of teams on social media postgame. In Week 3 of the NFL season, the Washington Commanders proved that assessment to be correct.

Washington defeated the Seattle Seahawks 33-31 on Sunday, snapping Seattle's 13-game win streak. The Commanders entered the game with backup quarterback Marcus Mariota under center due to Jayden Daniels' elbow injury.

Mariota delivered by throwing for 183 yards and three touchdowns. Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold started for the first time since an oblique injury forced him out in Week 1. Darnold had 379 passing yards and four touchdowns, but two interceptions -- the latter of which resulted in a pick-six with 3:57 left in the game.

The Commanders went straight to trolling after the win. They shared a video from the hit comedy show, "The Office," where Jim delivers coffee to Dwight. However, Dwight can only pick it up with his toes and ends up spilling the hot drink on himself. In this case, Jim is the Commanders, delivering an "L" to Dwight, the Seahawks.

Here are the top trolls from Week 3.

Pittsburgh Steelers 30, Cincinnati Bengals 27
An early season AFC North clash predictably went down to the wire.

Facing a three-point deficit with 2:15 left in the game, the Bengals received possession and started driving. They reached the Steelers' 38-yard-line, but Pittsburgh defensive tackle Derrick Harmon sacked quarterback Joe Burrow, resulting in a fumble that the Steelers recovered to win.

Ever the trollers, Pittsburgh wouldn't pass up on the opportunity to poke fun at its division rivals with cats being the theme. The Steelers posted a victory image with the caption: "meoW," a video of a cat doing a viral dance and another cat photo captioned: "raWr."

Buffalo Bills 24, Los Angeles Chargers 16
Buffalo stormed back to defeat Los Angeles and remain undefeated on the season.

The Bills began the fourth quarter down 13-10 and fumbled immediately. Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert then threw an interception three plays later, which the Bills capitalized on by scoring a touchdown to go ahead for good. They iced the win with a final drive with 1:56 left in the game.

Los Angeles is known for its elaborate social media posts when announcing its upcoming season's schedule. This year, they posted a Halo-themed video, which Buffalo referenced in its postgame jab.

Atlanta Falcons 35, Green Bay Packers 14
Atlanta is a winner for the first time this season following an emphatic "Thursday Night Football" performance in Green Bay.

The Falcons put up 498 total yards of offense, outscoring the Packers 35-7 after falling behind 7-0 midway through the first quarter. In his first start of the season, Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. threw for 256 yards and one touchdown, while running back Bijan Robinson had 213 total yards and two scores.

The big victory came with multiple trolls aimed at the Packers, including a spin on the "Go Pack Go" chant and a reference to rapper T-Pain's "Wiscansin" lyric.
